## Explore the weather data

Choose a city and measure from the menu inside the chart. The date-range slider lets you focus on a particular part of 2023. The readings are hourly observations, so zooming in reveals changes across individual hours rather than daily averages.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from datetime import datetime
from meteostat import config, hourly

config.block_large_requests = False

start = datetime(2023, 1, 1)
end = datetime(2023, 12, 31, 23, 59)

stations = {
    "Sarasota": "KSRQ0",
    "Ulaanbaatar": "44292",
}

records = []

for city, station in stations.items():
    weather = hourly(station, start, end).fetch()
    if weather is None or weather.empty:
        continue

    weather = weather.reset_index().rename(columns={"time": "date"})
    weather = weather[["date", "temp", "prcp"]].dropna().copy()
    weather["city"] = city
    weather["temp_f"] = (weather["temp"] * 9 / 5) + 32
    records.append(weather)

weather_data = pd.concat(records, ignore_index=True)

fig = go.Figure()
selections = [
    ("Sarasota", "Temperature", "temp_f", "Temperature (°F)", "#1C6E8C"),
    ("Sarasota", "Rainfall", "prcp", "Rainfall (mm)", "#D96C06"),
    ("Ulaanbaatar", "Temperature", "temp_f", "Temperature (°F)", "#1C6E8C"),
    ("Ulaanbaatar", "Rainfall", "prcp", "Rainfall (mm)", "#D96C06"),
]

for city, measure, column, y_title, color in selections:
    city_data = weather_data[weather_data["city"] == city]
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=city_data["date"],
            y=city_data[column],
            mode="lines",
            line={"color": color, "width": 1},
            name=f"{city} {measure}",
            visible=(city == "Sarasota" and measure == "Temperature"),
            hovertemplate="%{x|%b %d, %H:%M}<br>%{y:.1f}<extra></extra>",
        )
    )

buttons = []
for index, (city, measure, column, y_title, color) in enumerate(selections):
    visible = [False] * len(selections)
    visible[index] = True
    buttons.append(
        {
            "label": f"{city}: {measure}",
            "method": "update",
            "args": [
                {"visible": visible},
                {
                    "title": f"{city} hourly {measure.lower()} readings in 2023",
                    "yaxis": {"title": y_title},
                },
            ],
        }
    )

fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    title="Sarasota hourly temperature readings in 2023",
    width=950,
    height=560,
    hovermode="x unified",
    xaxis={
        "title": "Date and time",
        "rangeslider": {"visible": True},
        "rangeselector": {
            "buttons": [
                {"count": 1, "label": "1 month", "step": "month", "stepmode": "backward"},
                {"count": 3, "label": "3 months", "step": "month", "stepmode": "backward"},
                {"step": "all", "label": "All year"},
            ]
        },
    },
    yaxis={"title": "Temperature (°F)"},
    updatemenus=[
        {
            "buttons": buttons,
            "direction": "down",
            "showactive": True,
            "x": 0,
            "xanchor": "left",
            "y": 1.16,
            "yanchor": "top",
        }
    ],
    margin={"t": 120, "r": 30, "b": 80, "l": 70},
)
fig.show()
```

Use the menu to compare the two cities and switch between temperature and rainfall. Try narrowing the slider to winter or summer to see when the two places differ most.
